itsm._package: Interim PyPI package freshservice-mcp-ids 1.1.0 (https://pypi.org/project/freshservice-mcp-ids/) until upstream freshservice-mcp accepts group_id and responder_id on create_ticket. The console script stays freshservice-mcp. That package already caps mcp<1.9 and pydantic<2.14; the --with pins stay so a resolver change cannot pull the broken majors.
itsm._resultIsErrorWhen_note: This server catches its own failures and returns them as SUCCESSFUL tool results - isError is false and the message arrives as ordinary text, e.g. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: Either email or requester_id must be provided"}],"isError":false}. HTTP 400 from POST /tickets is different: create_ticket returns "Validation Error: ..." (observed 2026-10-21 on tooling-prod, logged as [executed] because the old pattern only matched a leading Error). Without this pattern executor.js believes it, so a rejected ticket is notified as executed. The regex is applied ONLY when the entire result is a bare string (see resultIsDeclaredError in executor.js), never to structured output, because a false positive is worse than the bug: it would report a completed action as failed and leave it in the approval queue for a retry that executes it twice. Remove this if upstream starts setting isError properly.
itsm._pin: THREE upstream problems, two pins. (1) freshservice-mcp 1.0.0 declares 'mcp[cli]>=1.3.0' with no upper bound, so uvx resolves mcp 2.0.0, which removed mcp.server.fastmcp - the server dies at import and mcpBackends.js reports a generic 'Connection closed'. Anything below 2 fixes that. (2) Below 2 is not enough: several of its tools are annotated as returning str but return a dict, and from ~1.9 the SDK derives an outputSchema from that annotation and validates against it, so get_ticket_by_id, get_list_of_solution_article and get_solution_article ALL failed with 'validation error ... Output'. Verified 2026-08-04 by flipping the pin on the running pod: under mcp<2 three of six mapped verbs were unusable, under mcp<1.9 all six work. Below 1.9 no outputSchema is emitted at all, so there is nothing to validate. The cost is no structuredContent on any result - tool output reaches the agents as text, which is what the bridge does with it anyway. (3) mcp 1.8.x imports eval_type_backport from pydantic._internal._typing_extra, which pydantic 2.14 removed - under mcp<1.9 alone uvx now resolves pydantic 2.14.x and the server dies at import with ImportError (observed 2026-10-20 on tooling-prod after the 0.12.1 roll: Teams 'schemas could not be resolved', bridge '[itsm] failed to connect: Connection closed'). Pin pydantic>=2.10,<2.14 alongside mcp<1.9; verified locally that freshservice-mcp starts (mcp 1.8.1 + pydantic 2.13.5). Revisit if upstream fixes its return annotations or moves off FastMCP v1, and note this re-resolves on every pod start, so a newly-cut major of any other unbounded dependency can break it again with no change on our side.
itsm._host: The host is a DEPLOYMENT fact, set by freshservice.domain in values.yaml, not baked in here. It was previously hardcoded to one tenant, which made this file unusable by anyone else and - worse - silently ignored the FRESHSERVICE_DOMAIN the ExternalSecret was already supplying. Two sources for one value, one of them dead. The chart now fails to render if the provider is selected and the domain is empty, rather than shipping a literal ${FRESHSERVICE_DOMAIN} to the API.
itsm._note: Self-hosted community server (github.com/effytech/freshservice_mcp, MIT), run via uvx - stdio transport, not a hosted remote endpoint. Freshworks does have its own native MCP integration, but as of writing it's Beta/EAP-gated to selected Enterprise-plan customers (see developers.freshworks.com/docs/agentic-dev-tools/mcp-server/) - this community server works today without needing that program. FRESHSERVICE_APIKEY comes from Profile Settings -> API Settings in the Freshservice admin panel.
itsm._verified: 2026-08-04: all 6 mapped verbs checked against a live tools/list from freshservice-mcp 1.0.0 (59 tools, confirmed identical from the deployed pod) - filter_tickets, get_ticket_by_id, get_list_of_solution_article, get_solution_article, create_ticket_note and create_ticket all exist. Re-run scripts/list-provider-tools.py freshservice after any version bump; it diffs the mapping against the running server and exits non-zero on a miss.
itsm._write_surface: Those 59 tools include ~20 that write or destroy - delete_ticket, update_ticket, create_service_request, create_agent, create_requester, and the whole solution-article set. Exactly 2 are mapped (create_ticket at tier_2, create_ticket_note at tier_2). The rest have no action-mapping entry and therefore cannot execute at all, which is the intended fail-closed state, NOT an oversight to be tidied up by adding mappings. Note delete_ticket in particular appears in no tier of policy/risk-tiers.yaml either, so it would also fall to default_policy.unlisted_action.
